A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LLaSE-G1 and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and Appendix A. Content can be reliably matched across the added subsection, table renumbering, and pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original speech-enhancement experiments, inference-time scaling, similarity measurements, and ablations in Section 4, Tables 2–8, and Figure 2.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds a subjective listening study and an additional input-representation ablation.

M1.justification: The WavLM–LLaMA–X-codec2 architecture, dual-channel design, losses, and inference procedures remain unchanged. Projection-head explanations and channel-label corrections clarify the existing method; the added token-input configuration is an experimental ablation.

E1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A.2 retain the training sources and all noise suppression, packet loss concealment, target speaker extraction, echo cancellation, and speech separation benchmarks. The listening study reuses DNS blind-test audio without introducing a new speech task or input scenario.

E2.justification: The matched ablation comparison adds an Xcodec2-token-input LLaMA variant in v3 Table 9, absent from v1 Table 8. External baseline membership in Tables 2–7 remains unchanged; the new subjective comparison reuses FRCRN, SELM, and GenSE and includes clean speech as a reference.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a five-point subjective MOS protocol with 12 participants listening to 50 samples each, plus the additional token-input ablation configuration. Existing training budgets, model sizes, benchmark settings, and inference procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 Table 9 extends the existing representation ablation by testing Xcodec2-token inputs with the LLaMA backbone, X-codec2 output, and single inference. This tests whether acoustically informed discrete inputs match continuous embeddings; the scaling and similarity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added listening study reports MOS point estimates without uncertainty; its participant and sample counts describe study size.

E6.justification: New Table 8 reports subjective MOS of 4.1208 for LLaSE-G1 and 4.0083 for GenSE. Table 9 adds OVRL 3.29 for Xcodec2-token inputs, alongside the retained continuous-input result of 3.43. Existing benchmark values and Figure 2 curves are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–3 retain the same probability formulation and losses. Correcting the reference-speech symbol and output-channel indices does not introduce new mathematical reasoning, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The core claims about acoustic preservation, unified enhancement, test-time scaling, and unseen-task generalization remain intact. The conclusion's explicit statement about requiring no task prompts reiterates the task-ID-free claim already present in v1's abstract and introduction.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the listening results as evidence of better perceptual detail preservation and the new ablation as showing information loss even with Xcodec2-token inputs. It also explicitly attributes reverberant performance to the continuous representations and decoder. The limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 clarifies that Table 7's noise-suppression results average reverberant and non-reverberant sets, expands the output-projection explanation, and identifies the appendix's input vector as a WavLM embedding. The first-page hyperlink changes from a demo page to a code repository. Training hardware and hyperparameters are unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and bibliography are unchanged, including the positioning against discriminative and generative enhancement systems. No cited work or substantive novelty relationship is added or removed.

P1.justification: v3 locally rewrites the noise-suppression discussion, target-speaker discussion, and conclusion, corrects terminology and notation, and inserts a subjective-evaluation subsection before the renumbered ablation subsection. The broader narrative and organization remain stable.

P2.justification: v3 adds the subjective MOS table and expands the former Table 8 into a wider Table 9 with explicit input names and another row. Figure 1 is resized and clarifies the two output branches; Table 7 gains an explanatory caption. Figure 2 remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: The listening study provides direct perceptual evidence beyond v1's automated metrics, while the added ablation better supports the continuous-input design. Clarified descriptions and access information also help readers assess the work. The gains are limited by sparse listening-study details and absent uncertainty estimates, so the revision supports a modest overall improvement.
